text:
If you’re heading onto the lake this afternoon, take the Lake Wind Advisory seriously. Burlington is living up to the forecast so far, cloudy and mainly dry at 72, but south winds are expected to build to 10 to 15 mph on land and 15 to 25 knots over the water. Waves will run 1 to 3 feet, so this is not a casual paddling window.

The afternoon should stay mostly dry, with a high near 77, but the weather turns sharply after sunset. Rain may begin around 7 or 8, then periods of heavier rain and embedded thunderstorms take over, with a half to three-quarters of an inch possible and gusts up to 30 mph. Tomorrow stays unsettled too, with showers and thunderstorms likely before 5 and a high near 79. Enjoy the dry stretch this afternoon, but be off the lake before evening and keep tonight’s plans close to home.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Wednesday! Our Wednesday starts cloudy and mainly dry, and through the bulk of the daytime hours today we keep the cloud cover but stay mainly dry. The better chance for rain and a few embedded thunderstorms comes later this evening after sunset into the night ahead. Afternoon high temperatures are generally in the low to mid 70s. Lows tonight fall into the 60s for most as the rain pushes through. Most places look to run between .25-.75″ of new rain, but localized higher totals of over 1″ are possible. There is also a low-end risk of a strong storm or two in southwestern St. Lawrence County.
